answer: In an AI-agent economy, Sybil resistance comes from bonded, slashable identity: each agent locks a stake before it can earn or vote, and a proven duplicate forfeits the whole stake. Cost scales with headcount while payout tracks verified work, so ten thousand fakes mean ten thousand bonds at risk for almost no yield. A per-agent behavioural fingerprint is the marble marking each identity unique, so a bridge reusing one bond across claims is caught and slashed, not a velvet ride. The attacker burns capital at total-loss risk, and break-even sits well above what a fake identity can extract.
